# Security, Reliability and Release Checklist: orca-server devcontainer Feature

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for secrets, entrypoint safety, pinning, idempotency, test coverage and publishing are complete, clear and consistent.
**Created**: 2026-11-23
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Depth**: standard release gate. **Audience**: reviewer at pull request and release. **Defaults used**: no clarifying questions were asked, because the request names its six focus areas.

**Tick record**: items ticked on 2026-11-23 at Dru's request, after the spec, plan and tasks were amended. Each item carries one line of evidence.

## Secrets and Pairing Links

- [x] CHK001 Are file permissions required for `/var/lib/orca-server/pairing-url.txt`, given that the link works like a password? [Gap, Spec Decision 10, FR-013] Evidence: spec FR-015 and Decision 18 set 0600 for the file and 0700 for the directory.
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec say how `/var/lib/orca-server/orca-server.log` is protected, when Orca writes the full pairing link to that log? [Gap, Spec FR-013] Evidence: spec Decision 17 and FR-015 set the log to 0600 in the volume, not in `/tmp`.
- [x] CHK003 Is "no secret in an image layer" defined for every file `install.sh` writes, including `options.env`, `remote-user` and the volume directory? [Completeness, Spec FR-022] Evidence: spec FR-022 lists every file `install.sh` writes.
- [x] CHK004 Is it stated that `TS_AUTH_KEY` and any Tailscale credential stay outside this Feature's files, logs and options? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases] Evidence: spec FR-022 says the Feature MUST NOT read, store or log `TS_AUTH_KEY`.
- [x] CHK005 Is the pairing link excluded from build-time output, so a build log cannot hold a link? [Gap, Spec FR-022] Evidence: spec FR-022 says `install.sh` MUST NOT start Orca and MUST NOT print a pairing link.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for who may run `orca-server url`, which creates access links? [Gap, Spec FR-023] Evidence: spec FR-023 limits it to the remote user and root through `runuser`.
- [x] CHK007 Is the effect of `--refuse-public` on clients behind a Docker port forward or Tailscale userspace networking stated as a requirement and not only in research? [Gap, Spec FR-025, Research D10] Evidence: spec FR-025 states the private-address and loopback cases.
- [x] CHK008 Are revocation requirements stated or explicitly excluded, given that grants live until revoked? [Assumption, Spec Context] Evidence: spec Assumptions say revoking a grant is done in Orca and is out of scope.

## Entrypoint and Container Start

- [x] CHK009 Is the 2 second limit measured from a defined start point and to a defined end point? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-012, AC 5] Evidence: spec FR-012 and AC 5 measure from the entrypoint start line to the line before `exec "$@"`.
- [x] CHK010 Does acceptance criterion 5 describe something the Feature controls, when `postStartCommand` timing belongs to the tool? [Ambiguity, Spec AC 5] Evidence: spec AC 5 now uses two timestamped log lines written by the entrypoint.
- [x] CHK011 Is a time limit defined for `tailscale status --json`, so a hung command cannot extend the wait past `tailscaleWaitSeconds`? [Gap, Spec Decision 5] Evidence: spec Decision 5 and FR-010 limit each call to 5 seconds.
- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for a second `start` while the first is still waiting for Tailscale? [Gap, Edge Case] Evidence: spec FR-027 (lock file) and the Edge Cases entry for a second `start`.
- [x] CHK013 Is the handling of a stale PID file (process gone, file present) specified? [Gap, Spec FR-016] Evidence: spec FR-016 says a stale PID file counts as stopped and is removed.
- [x] CHK014 Is the behaviour defined when Orca exits after it started successfully (crash, not port conflict)? [Gap, Recovery] Evidence: spec FR-018 and Edge Cases: log line, `status` stopped, no automatic restart.
- [x] CHK015 Is the interaction with other Feature entrypoints specified, and is it flagged as unverified? [Assumption, Research D7] Evidence: spec FR-009 and Assumptions state `exec "$@"` chaining and flag it unverified, with a test in tasks T038.
- [x] CHK016 Is "exactly one error line" in AC 6 consistent with FR-018, which also logs a port failure? [Consistency, Spec FR-011, FR-018, AC 6] Evidence: spec FR-018 uses the line `orca-server: orca-ide exited with status <n>`, which does not start with `orca-server: error:`.
- [x] CHK017 Does the spec define what `tailscaleWaitSeconds` set to 0 means? [Gap, Spec Decision 5] Evidence: spec Decision 5 and FR-010 say 0 means one check and no wait.
- [x] CHK018 Is the wait length consistent with the 90 second readiness limit in AC 3 and AC 4 when Tailscale is slow? [Conflict, Spec Decision 5 default 120, AC 3, AC 4] Evidence: spec Decision 5 skips the wait when `pairingAddress` is set, AC 3 and AC 4 use `pairingAddress`, and AC 13 covers the Tailscale path.

## Pinned Versions and Integrity

- [x] CHK019 Is the update procedure for the pinned version and hash defined (who bumps both, and how a mismatch with the JSON default is caught)? [Gap, Spec Decision 16] Evidence: spec FR-024 gives the one-commit bump and the `verify.sh fast` failure, and plan Decisions recorded item 9 gives the procedure.
- [x] CHK020 Is it stated whether `latest` bypasses the pinned hash, and which hash source applies? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-003, FR-024] Evidence: spec Decision 20 says a resolved version equal to the default uses the default hash, otherwise the API digest.
- [x] CHK021 Are failure requirements defined when the GitHub release API is unreachable, rate limited or returns no digest for a non-default version? [Gap, Spec Decision 16] Evidence: spec FR-003 (exit 2 for the release lookup) and FR-024 (exit 3 for unreachable, rate limited or no digest).
- [x] CHK022 Is the weaker guarantee for non-default versions recorded as a requirement-level limit and not only an assumption? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions] Evidence: spec FR-024 states the limit and the `debSha256` remedy.
- [x] CHK023 Is pinning required for the other downloaded artefacts, namely apt dependencies, the devcontainer CLI and `devcontainers/action`? [Gap, Constitution IV, Plan D8] Evidence: spec FR-029 pins the CLI, shellcheck, shfmt and actions, and states that apt dependencies resolve from the base distribution.
- [x] CHK024 Is the hash mismatch message format fixed in one place, and do FR-024 and the contract agree on it? [Consistency, Spec FR-024, Contracts] Evidence: spec FR-024 gives the exact line, and `contracts/feature-options.md` shows the same line.
- [x] CHK025 Are the install exit codes for unsupported base (1), missing asset (2) and hash mismatch (3) required by the spec and not only by the contract? [Consistency, Spec FR-004, FR-005, FR-024] Evidence: spec FR-004 (exit 1), FR-005 (exit 2) and FR-024 (exit 3) state them.

## Idempotent Install

- [x] CHK026 Is "same result" in FR-006 defined (files, ownership, installed version, options.env content)? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-006] Evidence: spec FR-006 defines same package version and same content, owner and mode for every file written.
- [x] CHK027 Is the behaviour defined when a second run uses a different `version` or different options? [Gap, Spec FR-006] Evidence: spec FR-006 says the new version installs in place and `options.env` is rewritten.
- [x] CHK028 Is the behaviour defined when the volume already exists with a different owner than the remote user? [Gap, Spec FR-015] Evidence: spec FR-015 says the entrypoint enforces owner and mode at each start.
- [x] CHK029 Is the behaviour defined when `_REMOTE_USER` is root or unset? [Gap, Spec Decision 11] Evidence: spec FR-014 and Edge Cases say `install.sh` exits 1 with one line.
- [x] CHK030 Are option validation rules (`port` range, `version` format, `tailscaleWaitSeconds` integer) required by the spec and not only by the data model? [Gap, Data Model] Evidence: spec FR-028 states the three rules and exit 1.

## Test Coverage of Acceptance Criteria

- [x] CHK031 Does each of the acceptance criteria have a named verification method (scenario, script or manual check)? [Traceability, Spec Acceptance Criteria] Evidence: plan.md Slice 4 table has one row per criterion 1 to 17.
- [x] CHK032 Are FR-023, FR-024 and FR-025 covered by an acceptance criterion, when the verbatim list has none for them? [Gap, Spec FR-023, FR-024, FR-025] Evidence: spec AC 14, 15 and 16 cover them, and AC 17 covers FR-026.
- [x] CHK033 Are the edge cases (port in use, restart without rebuild, install twice, non-root user, unsupported base) each tied to an acceptance criterion or a test? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases] Evidence: plan.md Slice 4 edge-case table maps each case to a script or task.
- [x] CHK034 Is the plan's test scope consistent with the acceptance criteria, with 9 and 12 named as manual or release checks? [Consistency, Plan Slice 4] Evidence: plan.md Slice 4 table lists criterion 9 as manual and 12 as the first release run.
- [x] CHK035 Can AC 9 (reconnect after rebuild) be objectively recorded as passed, given it is manual and needs a real client? [Measurability, Spec AC 9] Evidence: plan.md table and tasks T055 require date, client version and outcome in `docs/analysis/261123-orca-server-feature.md`.
- [x] CHK036 Can AC 12 be checked before the first publish, and is a dry run (`validate-only`) required? [Gap, Spec AC 12] Evidence: spec FR-030 and tasks T046 run the action in `validate-only` mode on pull requests.
- [x] CHK037 Is AC 4 ("one line that starts with a URL scheme") consistent with Decision 14, where the stored link is the mobile link by default? [Consistency, Spec AC 4, Decision 14] Evidence: both link kinds start with `orca://pair`, so AC 4 holds for the stored link (Decision 14, AC 14).
- [x] CHK038 Is a test environment without Tailscale defined for AC 6, and for AC 3, which needs a running Orca on a base image? [Dependency, Spec AC 3, AC 6] Evidence: plan.md Slice 4 table: AC 3 runs with `pairingAddress` set, and AC 6 runs on a base with no Tailscale.

## Publish and Permissions

- [x] CHK039 Are the required workflow permissions (`packages: write`, `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`) stated in the spec, and not only in the plan? [Gap, Plan D8] Evidence: spec FR-021 names all three.
- [x] CHK040 Is the repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" recorded as a prerequisite? [Dependency, Research D8] Evidence: spec Assumptions and tasks T051.
- [x] CHK041 Is package visibility required to be public, given that new GHCR packages are private by default and consumers cannot pull private Features? [Gap, Spec FR-021] Evidence: spec FR-026, Decision 19 and AC 17.
- [x] CHK042 Is "a push to main that changes the Feature version" defined precisely, including what happens when the version is unchanged? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-021] Evidence: spec FR-021 defines the trigger (changes under `src/orca-server/`) and says an unchanged version is skipped and the run succeeds.
- [x] CHK043 Is publishing required to depend on a passing test run? [Gap, Plan Slice 5] Evidence: spec FR-021 says publish only after the test workflow passes.
- [x] CHK044 Are the generated README and its pull request required to pass the same checks as other changes? [Gap, Spec FR-021] Evidence: spec FR-021 says Dru runs `bash scripts/verify.sh ci` on the README pull request branch, because `GITHUB_TOKEN` pull requests start no workflow.
- [x] CHK045 Is the minimum permission for `test.yaml` stated (read only, no secrets on fork pull requests)? [Gap, Plan Slice 4] Evidence: spec FR-030 says `contents: read` only and no secret.
- [x] CHK046 Is a rollback or withdrawal path defined for a bad published version? [Gap, Recovery] Evidence: spec FR-031 and tasks T049 define withdrawal by a fixed patch version and the package version deletion steps.
